implementation_notes: The same __builtin_prefetch intrinsic in C++, which maps to the platform instruction; there is no standard prefetch in C++ and the intrinsic is the portable-across-GCC/Clang spelling. On x86 the non-temporal prefetch (prefetchnta) is particularly useful for a write or a single-use read because it avoids the read-for-ownership that pollutes the cache - the classic case is filling a large buffer that will not be re-read. C++ adds the iterator-friendly form: computing an address one element ahead of an iterator in a strided loop and prefetching it is a two-line change that often removes most of the stall. The same vectorisation caveat applies: a prefetch inside the inner loop will stop the compiler from vectorising it, so it goes outside.
pitfalls: A prefetch inside the inner loop inhibits vectorisation - the hint and the wider type are a real trade.
There is no standard C++ prefetch; __builtin_prefetch is a compiler extension (works on GCC/Clang, not on MSVC, which has _mm_prefetch and _mm_prefetchw).
On x86, prefetcht2 / __builtin_prefetch(p,0,2) does not consistently mean L3 across vendors - tune on the target part.
Prefetching a pointer after dereferencing it (rather than prefetching the pointer's target) hides nothing - the address must be known before the load that needs it.
